original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Can scripts/exclusion_circuit.py:ExclusionCircuit.verify_embedding replace its reverse-frame expected-support genexpr with an equivalent closed-form sorted-output mask (full ^ (vertex[a]|vertex[b])) so verify_embedding receipts and every forward/reverse nesting assertion stay fieldwise identical on the historical n=45 circuit, without changing ExclusionCircuit.verify's leave-two-out path?
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one measured replay bottleneck with before/after wall time and retained checks. Expertise override selected verifier-engineering after open tooling PR #2001 left ExclusionCircuit.verify_embedding's reverse-frame expected-support sum as an explicit next question (distinct from that PR's verify leave-two-out object). Profiling named that genexpr as the verify_embedding hot path.
bottleneck_link: Side result on review throughput: reversible-embedding checks and any callers of ExclusionCircuit.verify_embedding pay the reverse-frame expected-support sum. A faster identical embedding receipt does not change kappa or the binding complex supplier.
stop_rule: Ship an equivalence-preserving ExclusionCircuit.verify_embedding reverse-mask change with frozen baseline, identical receipts on the historical n=45 circuit, updated source pins only on the four binding certificates, registered replay and a measured before/after median. Co-land with #2001's verify leave-two-out rewrite in one production pin; do not reopen mathematical screens or run the selected cold frontier replay.
evidence: PASS_EXCLUSION_EMBEDDING_MASKS via research/exclusion-embedding-masks/verify.py (also under -O); PASS_IDENTICAL_EXCLUSION_EMBEDDING_MASK_RECEIPTS via benchmark.py; four certificates differ from base only in the scripts/exclusion_circuit.py source pin.
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for orientation, overlap search, profiling, implementation, packaging, benchmarking and writing. Not independent human peer review.

open_questions.question: Should research/bit-compression-provenance and other packages that pin live scripts/exclusion_circuit.py bytes refresh those SHA-256 entries after this equivalence-preserving rewrite?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those provenance packages bind working-tree bytes; leaving the old pin keeps this tooling PR focused, but a later full provenance replay on main would see a hash mismatch until refreshed.
open_questions.first_step: Open a dedicated provenance follow-up that only rewrites the exclusion_circuit.py entry in those SOURCES/SOURCE-PINS files after confirming embedding receipts stay identical.
open_questions.blocked_by: Pin repair outside the four binding certificates is outside this tooling change.

open_questions.question: When open #2001 (verify leave-two-out masks) and this verify_embedding rewrite both land, should maintainer merge resolve scripts/exclusion_circuit.py by keeping both closed forms in one file with a single updated source pin?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Both PRs edit the same historical checker for different methods; certificate pins will need one combined hash after merge.
open_questions.first_step: Rebase the later PR onto the earlier merge commit and re-hash scripts/exclusion_circuit.py once.
open_questions.blocked_by: Resolved by folding into #2001's production file with a single updated source pin.
